parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A remote-controlled toy aircraft is flying horizontally in a wind. Fig. 3.1 shows the velocity vectors, to scale, of the wind and of the aircraft in still air.
{{figure:9702_w21_23_q03_figure_3_1}}
The velocity of the aircraft in still air is $42\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the north. The velocity of the wind is $23\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in a direction of $54^{\circ}$ east of south.
Determine the magnitude of the resultant velocity of the aircraft.

parts.label: (c)
parts.part_stem:
The engine of the aircraft in (b) stops. The aircraft then glides towards the ground with a constant velocity at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, as illustrated in Fig. 3.2.
{{figure:9702_w21_23_q03_figure_3_2}}
The aircraft has a weight of $46\text{ N}$ and travels a distance of $280\text{ m}$ from point $X$ to point $Y$. The change in gravitational potential energy of the aircraft for its movement from $X$ to $Y$ is $6100\text{ J}$.
Assume that there is now no wind.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the magnitude of the force acting on the aircraft due to air resistance.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The aircraft in (c) travels from $X$ to $Y$ in a time of $14\text{ s}$. Fig. 3.3 shows that, as the aircraft travels from $X$ to $Y$, it moves directly towards an observer who is standing on the ground.
{{figure:9702_w21_23_q03_figure_3_3}}
The aircraft emits sound as it travels from $X$ to $Y$. The observer hears sound of frequency $450\text{ Hz}$. The speed of the sound in the air is $340\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate the frequency of the sound that is emitted by the aircraft.
